capabilities: Sync vaults across devices via personal OneDrive, SharePoint document libraries, or Teams Files
Share individual vaults with colleagues granting read/write or read-only access
Automatically 3-way merge concurrent edits using eTags instead of creating conflict files
Browse and restore previous note revisions with author, email, and timestamp
Optionally sync shared themes, snippets, hotkeys, and plugins while excluding OAuth tokens and workspace layout
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff; deeper technical details are deferred to an ARCHITECTURE.md file rather than the README.
intentEvidence: Official Obsidian Sync requires a separate subscription and stores vault data outside your organization's Microsoft 365 tenant.
motivation: The author wanted to bring a OneNote-on-SharePoint workflow to Obsidian, where notebooks live inside Microsoft 365 teams with access control and built-in version history.
problem: Obsidian's own sync requires a paid subscription and stores data outside the Microsoft 365 tenant, while OneDrive desktop syncing creates duplicate conflict files.

relations.evidence: Official Obsidian Sync requires a separate subscription and stores vault data outside your organization's Microsoft 365 tenant.
talks directly to the Microsoft Graph API from Obsidian—no extra servers to host
frequently creates Note (Work PC's conflicted copy).md duplicates whenever two people edit a note

requires.name: Microsoft account (personal or corporate Entra ID)
Entra ID app registration created by an organization admin (enterprise use)

summary: Vault sync backed by OneDrive, SharePoint, and Microsoft Teams via Microsoft Graph, with per-vault sharing, 3-way merge, and version history.
